docs.title: applying first principles to keyboards
docs.text:
• first principles

Here’s a detailed 7-step process for first principles thinking:

  1. Define the Problem Clearly:
  2. the problem is we need to input content into a computer to communicate

  3. the problem is we need to input commands into a computer to have it do work

  4. Gather Existing Knowledge and Assumptions:

  5. Identify the current information, beliefs, or practices around this issue. What do people generally assume is true?
  6. people do not want to put in the effort most have stockholm syndrome they do not realize they are suffering
  7. to realize how bad a keyboard sucks you have to experience with your hands what a correctly engineered keyboard is like
  8. people do not think it is worth the effort to learn to use a keyboard that is designed correctly
  9. we could use voice recognition
  10. i can type faster than i think plus i tried voice and it still sucks

  11. also i don't want to hear everyone around me yapping at a computer with their mouth

  12. Challenge Every Assumption:

  13. Systematically question these assumptions. Ask yourself why things are done a certain way and if these assumptions are necessary or true.
  14. people who designed mechanical typewriters had problem figuring out how to prevent "tyepbars" from interfering with each other
  15. their solution was to move the keyboard layout around to fit the anatomy of the mechanical typewriter
  16. computer keyboards do not have "typebars" under the keys
  17. computers are not mechanical typewriters

  18. computers can have a keyboard that is designed to fit human anatomy there is no reason to stagger the keys around

  19. Break Down the Problem to its Basic Elements:

    • the problem is the keyboard should fit human anatomy
    • our arms are spread apart the keyboard should be two pieces so you can place them at the width of your shoulders
    • our thumbs have a wider range of motion so we can utilize thumbs for mor than just a spacebar
    • our fingers have different lengths the keys should accomodate that anatomy
    • software allows moving keys under the fingers eliminating the need to place any keys beyond reach of the fingers

  20. Understand Why These Fundamentals are True:

  21. Validate why the basic elements you've identified are true. Are they based on evidence, or are they assumptions that you mistakenly accepted?

  22. machines should perform effort for humans not the other way around

  23. Reconstruct from First Principles:

  24. Build your understanding or solution from the ground up, using only the core truths identified in the previous steps. Work upwards logically without letting conventional thinking influence your approach.
  25. how many thumbs do we have? 1 per hand
  26. how many fingers do we have? 4 per hand
  27. how many keys can the thumb reach comfortably? 3
  28. how many keys can the inner fingers reach comfortably? 1 each + 1 upwards + 1 downwards

  29. how many keys can the outtermost fingers reach comfortably? 1 each + 1 upwards + 1 downwards + 3 to the left or right

  30. Develop and Test New Solutions:

  31. Once you’ve restructured the problem using first principles, brainstorm novel solutions and test them rigorously. The goal is to arrive at approaches that are more efficient, innovative, or accurate based on your fresh understanding.
  32. this problem was already solved there are many programmable keyboards

this year (2026) I sold my motorcycle because I found an amazing deal on a vespa gts 250ie which has more torque and hp plus is an automatic and a step through

fun fact this is my 6th vespa and 9th scooter

I wanted to get more exercise so I used the motorcycle money to build some advanced modern longboards

docs.title: surfskate
docs.text:
surfskate boards you can say are low geared and turn extremely sharp similar to a surfing you can "pump" it to accelerate from a stand still

on most of my surfskates you can tune the angle of the rear truck which holds the wheels on the board so the gearing changes and it feels like a shorter or longer surfboard

when you ride a surfskate downhill you have to keep the speed down so you turn back and forth aka switchback carving

I recently built a downhill slalom racing board I will add a video of that later

on flat land you can move in a rhythm back and forth to pump it forward without removing your feet from the board you can even do this up small hills

a ldp aka long board pump longboard is setup for efficient and comfortable long distances high geared pumping so you push up to speed then maintain the speed using rhythmic motions

a pump track is similar to a roller coaster and you can accelerate by compressing and decompressing your knees in rhythm

docs.title: my longboard stories
docs.text:
fun fact - I'm 53 and I started skateboarding (again)

I am trying to keep it safe for example drive to the burke gilman and use a long distance pumper the biggest danger there are the morons in spandex or the mob flying around on ebike motorcycles or onewheels I have nothing against ebikes etc. but if you are going over the trail limit which is 15mph you need to go ride on the street with the cars not the grandmas with baby strollers

that said my downhill slalom board is so stable I find my self going increasingly fast and loving it lol

I started skateboarding in elementary school my mom got me I believe a variflex with bennett trucks

I used to get an exhilarating feeling carving on it - carving is leaning hard into curves

now I have a custom modified slalom racing bennett truck and learned why it used to be so exhilarating

they have a design that causes a high rate "divey" turning profile

I skated everywhere!

I bicycled before that and I cannot remember what happened to my bmx bike

I either lost it or it broke but it never occurred to me to ask for another bike I just switched to skateboarding

later I upgraded it to a powell lance mountain which is a high value collector now I should have kept mine lol

I don't know what happened to that board I think I traded it for a per welinder then a skull freestyle deck and probably gave that away or lost it in a move

anyway I am not sure why I ever quit skating I did not get bored with it I wish I'd stuck with it

one reason I took a break is I broke my wrist bones and had a compound fracture but that was being dump I tried riding vert ramps with no training lol

docs.title: kingpins
docs.text:
AN6-22A: 3 AN6-23A: 3 AN6-24A: 7 AN6-25A: 4 AN6-26A: 2 AN6-27A: 1

Total unique AN part numbers: 6

The standard diameter for a skateboard or longboard kingpin is 3/8", which equals 6/16"—making all standard 3/8" longboard kingpins AN6 bolts (AN5 is 5/16", which is used for wheel axles, not kingpins).

The updated AN6 bolt sizes and sources:

Randal R2 Kingpin: AN6-25A (2 3/4") or AN6-27A (2 7/8") Kingpin Type: Reverse Kingpin (RKP) RipTide Bushing Height: 0.60" Standard Longboard

Paris V3 Kingpin: AN6-24A or AN6-25A Kingpin Type: Reverse Kingpin (RKP) RipTide Bushing Height: 0.60" Boardside / 0.50" Roadside

Paris Savant Kingpin: AN6-24A or AN6-25A Kingpin Type: Precision Reverse Kingpin (RKP) RipTide Bushing Height: 0.60" Standard Longboard

Dont Trip Poppy Kingpin: AN6-24A (2 9/16") Kingpin Type: Precision RKP with Spherical Pivot RipTide Bushing Height: 0.60" Standard Longboard

Dont Trip Slalocybin Kingpin: AN6-23A (2 1/2") or AN6-26A (2 13/16") Kingpin Type: Precision Slalom RKP RipTide Bushing Height: 0.75" Tall Longboard

Synergy Chorus Rear Kingpin: AN6-22A (2 5/16") or AN6-23A Kingpin Type: Precision Adjustable LDP Inverted Kingpin RipTide Bushing Height: 0.75" Tall or 0.60" Standard depending on setup

Zealous V2 Kingpin: AN6-24A Kingpin Type: Precision Slalom / Downhill RKP RipTide Bushing Height: 0.75" Tall Boardside / 0.50" Street Roadside

Valkyrie Mk4 Kingpin: AN6-24A or AN6-25A Kingpin Type: Precision RKP RipTide Bushing Height: 0.75" Tall Longboard

Bennett Vector Kingpin: AN6-23A (2 1/2") Kingpin Type: Traditional Kingpin (TKP) High Rake RipTide Bushing Height: 0.75" Tall Boardside / 0.50" Street Roadside

Sources & Sizing Reference:

  • Sk8Kings Aircraft Bolt Sizing Matrix (cross-references AN6 bolt lengths to Bennett, Don't Trip, Randal, and Tracker setups).
